topic: Claude Advisor Tool API: Mid-Generation Intelligence for Long-Horizon Tasks
keyword: Claude Advisor Tool API mid-generation intelligence 2026

competitors.title: Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform
key_points: Three new features: Tool Search Tool (on-demand tool discovery), Programmatic Tool Calling (code-orchestrated tools), Tool Use Examples (concrete usage patterns)
Tool Search Tool reduces context consumption from ~77K tokens to ~8.7K tokens, preserving 95% of context window — an 85% reduction
Internal testing: Opus 4 improved from 49% to 74% and Opus 4.5 from 79.5% to 88.1% on MCP evaluations with Tool Search Tool
Programmatic Tool Calling reduces average token usage from 43,588 to 27,297 (37% reduction) on complex research tasks
Knowledge retrieval improved from 25.6% to 28.5%, GIA benchmarks from 46.5% to 51.2% with programmatic tool calling
BrowseComp and DeepSearchQA benchmarks improved 11% while using 24% fewer input tokens with programmatic tool calling

competitors.title: Building Effective AI Agents
key_points: Defines the orchestrator-workers workflow: central LLM dynamically breaks down tasks, delegates to worker LLMs, and synthesizes results
Key distinction: workflows (predefined code paths) vs agents (LLMs dynamically direct their own processes)
Evaluator-optimizer workflow: one LLM generates, another provides evaluation and feedback in a loop
Three core principles: maintain simplicity, prioritize transparency, carefully craft agent-computer interface (ACI)
Augmented LLM as basic building block: LLM enhanced with retrieval, tools, and memory

competitors.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
key_points: Context engineering: curating the optimal set of tokens during LLM inference for desired behavior
Three techniques for long-horizon tasks: compaction, structured note-taking, and multi-agent architectures
Compaction: distills critical details (architectural decisions, unresolved bugs) while discarding redundant tool outputs
Structured note-taking: agentic memory persisted outside context window, pulled back in when needed
Sub-agent architectures: specialized sub-agents handle focused tasks with clean context windows, return 1,000-2,000 token summaries

competitors.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
key_points: Multi-agent system outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2% on internal research eval
Token usage explains 80% of performance variance in BrowseComp evaluation; number of tool calls and model choice explain remaining 15%
Multi-agent systems use ~15× more tokens than chat interactions, requiring high-value tasks for economic viability
Lead agent spawns specialized subagents (3-5) in parallel; subagents use 3+ tools in parallel — cuts research time up to 90%
Extended thinking mode serves as controllable scratchpad for planning and evaluation
Scale effort to query complexity: simple fact-finding = 1 agent with 3-10 calls; complex research = 10+ subagents

competitors.title: Programmatic Tool Calling — Anthropic Docs
key_points: Programmatic tool calling enables Claude to call tools from within code execution, not just direct API round-trips
Allowed_callers field controls which contexts can invoke a tool: direct, code_execution, or both
Container lifecycle: 30-day max lifetime, cleaned after 4.5 min idle, reuse via container ID
Supports Claude Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, 4.5 and Sonnet 4.6, 4.5 models
Ideal for large data processing, multi-step workflows with 3+ dependent calls, and parallel operations across many items

angles: The Advisor Pattern: How Opus-as-planner with Sonnet/Haiku execution creates a cost-efficient mid-generation intelligence layer for complex tasks
From orchestrator-workers to the Advisor API: How Anthropic's three new tool features (Tool Search, Programmatic Calling, Tool Use Examples) combine to enable the advisor pattern at API level
Context engineering for long-horizon tasks: Compaction, structured note-taking, and sub-agent architectures as the three pillars for managing attention budgets beyond single context windows
Token economics of the Advisor strategy: Why spending 19× more on Opus planning pays off through cheaper Haiku execution and 37% fewer overall tokens
Tool discovery as a first-class capability: How on-demand tool loading through Tool Search Tool transforms MCP-powered systems from context-bloated to lean
The programmatic orchestration revolution: Why expressing tool workflows in code (not natural language) yields 11% better benchmark performance with 24% fewer tokens
Scaling intelligence: When to use 1 agent vs 10+ subagents — a framework for matching effort to query complexity
CI/CD for agentic workflows: How to debug, evaluate, and deploy multi-agent systems with rainbow deployments and LLM-as-judge evaluation
outline: Introduction: What is the Claude Advisor Tool API and why mid-generation intelligence matters for long-horizon tasks
The Problem: Context bloat, tool selection errors, and inference overhead in complex multi-step workflows
The Advisor Pattern: Opus-planner + Sonnet/Haiku-executor model — cost savings (11%) with quality improvements
Tool Search Tool: On-demand tool discovery reducing context from 77K to 8.7K tokens with 85% savings
Programmatic Tool Calling: Code-orchestrated tools reducing token usage by 37% while improving benchmark performance
Tool Use Examples: Concrete usage patterns that go beyond JSON schema to teach correct tool invocation
The Three Context Engineering Strategies for Long-Horizon Tasks: Compaction, structured note-taking, and sub-agent architectures
Building a Multi-Agent System with the Advisor Pattern: Lead agent planning, sub-agent delegation, result synthesis
Token Economics: Cost analysis of Opus vs Haiku, when the advisor pattern pays off, and break-even calculations
Evaluation and Debugging: LLM-as-judge evaluation, rainbow deployments, production tracing for non-deterministic systems
When to Use the Advisor Pattern: Decision framework based on task complexity, parallelizability, and value per token
Conclusion: How mid-generation intelligence patterns will evolve with increasingly capable models
